title: Response caching: exact match and semantic (pgvector)
goal: Skip the model for repeated questions. An exact-match cache in Redis serves byte-identical temperature-0 requests; a semantic cache in Postgres (pgvector, HNSW) serves near-duplicates above a similarity threshold. Then make it give a wrong answer, and put the guards back.

changes.note: Exact cache keyed by tenant + model version + canonical request; embeddings via llama.cpp; nearest neighbour with pgvector; TTL jitter.
Lookups before the rate limit; single-flight for identical in-flight requests; store only finished (stop) answers.
POST /admin/similarity returns the cosine similarity of two texts.
pgvector extension, semantic_cache table, HNSW index on cosine distance, scope index.
embed service (llama.cpp --embeddings, bge-small-en-v1.5); postgres image switches to pgvector/pgvector:0.8.0-pg17.

run.label: Download the embedding model and start fresh (the database image changed)
run.cmd: ./scripts/download-models.sh && docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d --build

verify.label: Exact hit
verify.cmd: for i in 1 2; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-lab-acme-0001' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is HTTP?"}],"temperature":0,"max_tokens":60}' | grep -iE 'x-cache|x-replica'; done
verify.expect: First: x-replica (a model ran, no x-cache header). Second: x-cache: exact-hit, in milliseconds.

verify.label: Sampled requests are never cached
verify.cmd: curl -s -D - -o /dev/null localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-lab-acme-0001' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is HTTP?"}],"temperature":0.7,"max_tokens":60}' | grep -i x-cache
verify.expect: No output: temperature 0.7 skips the cache.

verify.label: Measure two similar prompts
verify.cmd: curl -s localhost:8091/admin/similarity -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"a":"How do I enable two-factor authentication?","b":"How do I disable two-factor authentication?"}'
verify.expect: {"similarity":0.9...,"threshold":0.95,"dimensions":384}. Write the number down: opposite intents, very close vectors.

verify.label: Semantic hit (opt-in)
verify.cmd: for q in 'How do I enable two-factor authentication?' 'How can I enable two-factor authentication?'; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-lab-acme-0001' -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-semantic-cache: allow' -d "{\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"$q\"}],\"temperature\":0,\"max_tokens\":60}" | grep -iE 'x-cache'; done
verify.expect: First: no x-cache (generated and stored). Second: x-cache: semantic-hit plus x-cache-similarity, if the two phrasings score above 0.95 on your run.

verify.label: Make it lie
verify.cmd: SEMANTIC_THRESHOLD=0.85 docker compose up -d gateway-a gateway-b && sleep 5 && curl -s localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-lab-acme-0001' -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-semantic-cache: allow' -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"How do I disable two-factor authentication?"}],"temperature":0,"max_tokens":60}'
verify.expect: If the enable/disable similarity you measured is above 0.85, the answer about ENABLING comes back for a question about DISABLING, with x-cache: semantic-hit. Then restore: docker compose up -d gateway-a gateway-b.

verify.label: Scoped by tenant
verify.cmd: curl -s -D - -o /dev/null localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-lab-globex-0001' -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-semantic-cache: allow' -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"How do I enable two-factor authentication?"}],"temperature":0,"max_tokens":60}' | grep -i x-cache
verify.expect: No output: globex cannot hit acme's entries, even for the identical question.

verify.label: Inspect the vectors
verify.cmd: docker compose exec postgres psql -U app -d llm -c "SELECT tenant_id, model_version, left(prompt, 50), vector_dims(embedding) FROM semantic_cache"
verify.expect: One row per stored answer, vector_dims 384, all with the current model_version.

concepts.how: Cache-aside: the gateway reads the cache, falls back to the model, then writes the answer back.
Stampede: single-flight coalesces identical in-flight requests; TTL jitter prevents synchronized expiry (avalanche).
The model version is in every key: a rollout invalidates by construction instead of by purge.
bge-small embeddings, cosine distance, an HNSW index in pgvector, filtering by tenant and model version.
Semantic caching's real trade-off: hit rate against wrong answers, and why the exact cache goes first.
Embed, index, nearest-neighbour search: the same retrieval machinery RAG uses, here returning answers instead of documents.
pgvector turns Postgres into a vector search index next to your relational data.
Scope by tenant so one customer's cached answer can never be served to another.

checkpoints.text: The second identical temperature-0 request returned x-cache: exact-hit.
I measured the similarity of 'enable' vs 'disable' 2FA with /admin/similarity.
I produced a wrong semantic hit by lowering the threshold, then restored it.
I confirmed a different tenant cannot hit another tenant's semantic entries.
